title: Uffici plugin install manifest
description: What `uffici setup` needs to install a plugin into its harness: where the harness keeps plugins, how to enable one, which configuration keys to set, and which environment the plugin reads. Carried at the top of every plugin release tarball as `uffici-plugin.json`. The companion holds no per-harness branch of its own: everything harness-specific is here, and a field the companion does not know is refused rather than ignored, because an ignored field would silently skip an install step.

harness.description: The harness kind, as the portal names it (`hermes`). The plugin's repository is `uffici-for-<harness>`.

name.description: The plugin's name in the harness's own registry — what `enable` names.

version.description: Stamped by the release from its tag; `0.0.0` in the tracked file.

pluginDir.description: Where the tarball's plugin directory is copied, relative to the harness home: at least two segments, none starting with a dot, and the last one the plugin's name — so a bad manifest can never name the harness's whole plugin folder.

homeEnv.description: The environment variable naming the harness home (`HERMES_HOME`).

defaultHome.description: The harness home when the variable is unset; a leading `~` is the user's home.

enable.description: The command that enables the plugin, as argv. Its first word must be on the PATH.

configSet.description: The argv prefix that sets one configuration key; the key and value are appended.

config.description: Configuration keys the harness must carry for the plugin to run.

envPath.description: An argv that prints the path of the harness's environment file. When absent, `envFile` under the harness home is used.

envFile.description: The environment file's name under the harness home, when `envPath` is absent or fails. Default `.env`.

env.description: The variables the plugin reads, with `${wireSocket}`, `${wireTokenFile}`, `${companionHome}` and `${home}` substituted by the companion.

restart.description: One sentence the person is told after the install, saying how to make the harness load the plugin.

restartCommand.description: The argv that restarts the harness when it runs as a service, which `uffici upgrade` runs after installing a new plugin. It must return once the restart is done. It runs only when `restartService` names a service definition that exists on this machine and the harness home is `defaultHome`; otherwise the person is told `restart`, because a restart command for a harness run by hand may start it in the foreground.

restartService.description: The harness's own service definition for `defaultHome`, per service manager: the systemd user unit's name (without `.service`) and the launchd agent's label. Its file existing is what makes `restartCommand` safe to run.
